newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr above 125 yen would cause friction with US-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Dlr above 125 yen would cause friction with US-MOF.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday that a dollar rate above 125 yen would cause trade friction with the United States.

Mitsuzuka told a key parliamentary committee that U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers told him that the United States was worried that Japan's growing trade surplus could cause trade or economic friction.
"It has been said that a currency rate above 125 yen would cause such things to happen. I think so too. This is the upper limit," he said.
Mitsuzuka said he told Summers that Japan will carry out various reforms mapped out by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's government.

Mitsuzuka also said he was asked by Summers about Japan's domestic demand-led growth, but told him that the Japanese government had no intention at the moment to take fiscal steps to stimulate the economy.
"Now is not the time to take fiscal steps," he said.
